plan: [ This is effectively a second‑price auction: the highest bid wins and pays the second-highest bid (exit price of the second-to-last bidder). In such auctions, bidding your true private value is a weakly dominant strategy, maximizing expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Underbidding risks losing profitable wins; overbidding risks paying more than value if a rival’s bid lies between your value and your overstated bid. With value $19 and no history (single round), bid exactly 19 to capture positive surplus when competitors’ top bid is below 19 while avoiding overpayment. ]

[ This two-stage format with auto-exit at sealed bids and payment equal to the second-highest bid is strategically equivalent to a second-price (Vickrey) auction. With independent private values and risk neutrality, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value: it maximizes expected profit, avoids profitable deviations, and removes downside risk of overbidding. There’s only 1 round, so no cross-round learning or signaling benefits from shading. Ties are random, so no advantage from tiny tweaks. I will bid exactly my value. ]

[ This is effectively a second-price auction: highest sealed bid wins and pays the second-highest bid. With independent private values, truthful bidding is a dominant strategy that maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Overbidding risks paying more than value if I win; underbidding risks losing when profitable. Since it’s only 1 round and values are i.i.d. uniform in [0,49], I will bid my true value of 43 to ensure I win exactly when price is below my value and avoid negative surplus. ]
